question: The concept of ‘Independence of judiciary’ in the Indian Constitution is taken from the Constitution of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is The USA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The framers of the Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of Independence of the Judiciary from the Constitution of the USA. (न्यायपालिका की स्वतंत्रता — संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका)

 

• Along with judicial independence, India also adopted Judicial Review, the Fundamental Rights (Bill of Rights), and the concept of the Supreme Court from the American Constitution.

 

• Independence of the judiciary means the judiciary is free from interference by the executive and the legislature, ensuring impartial dispensation of justice and protection of the Constitution.

 

• The Indian Constitution is often called a 'bag of borrowings' because it drew features from constitutions of several countries while adapting them to Indian conditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• From Britain, India borrowed the Parliamentary form of government, rule of law, single citizenship, and the concept of the Speaker.

 

• From Ireland, India borrowed the Directive Principles of State Policy and the method of election of the President.

 

• From Canada, India borrowed a quasi-federal system with a strong centre and the concept of residuary powers.

 

NOTE

 

• Ireland (Option 1): Contributed the Directive Principles of State Policy, not judicial independence.

 

• France (Option 2): Contributed the ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity in the Preamble.

 

• Britain (Option 4): Contributed the parliamentary system of government, not the independence of judiciary.

question: Which state in India was the most transformed by the Green Revolution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Punjab was the state most transformed by the Green Revolution, which began in India in the mid-1960s under the leadership of agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan. (हरित क्रांति — पंजाब)

 

• The Green Revolution introduced High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds (especially of wheat), along with chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and assured irrigation, dramatically boosting foodgrain production.

 

• Punjab's fertile alluvial soil, extensive canal and tube-well irrigation network, and early adoption of HYV wheat made it the epicentre of the revolution, earning it the title 'Granary/Food Bowl of India'.

 

• The Green Revolution helped India move from a food-deficit nation dependent on imports (like PL-480 wheat from the USA) to self-sufficiency in foodgrains by the early 1970s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Haryana was the second most benefited state from the Green Revolution, also seeing major gains in wheat production.

 

• The Green Revolution mainly boosted wheat and rice yields but had limited impact on pulses and oilseeds, and it is criticised for causing regional imbalance and soil/groundwater degradation in Punjab.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 1): Known instead for land reforms and high social development indicators, not the Green Revolution.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): More associated with the White Revolution (Operation Flood) and sugarcane cultivation.

 

• West Bengal (Option 3): Benefited less from the Green Revolution compared to Punjab due to different agro-climatic and land-holding conditions.

question:
Match the points under Column A with those under Column B.

Column A (Subphylum)

i. Hexapoda

ii. Crustacea

iii. Myriapoda

iv. Chelicerata

Column B (Animal)

a. Daphnia

b. Mosquito

c. Limulus

d. Julus
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-b, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All four subphyla of Phylum Arthropoda are correctly matched with their example animals. (संधिपाद प्राणी — उपसंघ वर्गीकरण)

 

• Hexapoda (i) includes insects, which have three pairs of legs; Mosquito (b) is a classic example of this subphylum.

 

• Crustacea (ii) includes mostly aquatic arthropods with two pairs of antennae; Daphnia (a), the 'water flea', is a well-known crustacean.

 

• Myriapoda (iii) includes many-legged arthropods like centipedes and millipedes; Julus (d) is a genus of millipede.

 

• Chelicerata (iv) includes arthropods with chelicerae (pincer-like mouthparts) such as spiders, scorpions and horseshoe crabs; Limulus (c), the horseshoe crab, belongs here.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Arthropoda is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, characterised by a chitinous exoskeleton, jointed appendages, and a segmented body.

 

• Other subphyla-level groupings used in classification include Trilobita (extinct marine arthropods).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-b, ii-c, iii-a, iv-d): Wrongly places Daphnia under Myriapoda and Limulus under Crustacea.

 

• Option 2 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Wrongly places Mosquito under Crustacea and Daphnia under Hexapoda.

 

• Option 3 (i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a): Wrongly places Julus under Hexapoda and Mosquito under Myriapoda.

question: Which of the following parts of the mountain will receive the most rainfall from moisture-laden winds?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Windward side.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The windward side of a mountain, the slope facing the incoming moisture-laden wind, receives the most rainfall. (पवनाभिमुख ढाल — सर्वाधिक वर्षा)

 

• As moist air is forced to rise along the windward slope, it cools adiabatically, condenses, and produces heavy orographic (relief) rainfall.

 

• After crossing the peak, the now largely dry air descends the other side, warming up and causing little to no rain — this drier zone is the leeward side, often called a rain-shadow area.

 

• A classic Indian example is the Western Ghats: the western (windward) slopes facing the Arabian Sea receive very heavy rainfall, while the eastern (leeward) side, including the Deccan Plateau, remains comparatively dry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This type of rainfall caused by forced ascent of air over mountains is called orographic or relief rainfall.

 

• The Cherrapunji-Mawsynram region in Meghalaya, on the windward side of the Khasi Hills facing the Bay of Bengal, is among the wettest places on Earth.

 

NOTE

 

• Leeward side (Option 2): Lies in the rain shadow and receives very little rainfall, the opposite of what the question asks.

 

• Upward side (Option 3): Not a standard geographical term used to describe mountain slopes in this context.

 

• Relief side (Option 4): 'Relief' describes the type of rainfall (relief/orographic rainfall), not a named slope of the mountain.

question: In the context of vernier calliper, an internal jaw is used to measure:
option_1: the length correct up to 1 mm
option_3: the length of a rod and diameter of a sphere
option_4: the internal diameter of a hollow cylinder and pipes
solution_text:
The correct answer is the internal diameter of a hollow cylinder and pipes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A vernier calliper has two pairs of jaws — external (lower) jaws and internal (upper) jaws — plus a depth probe. (वर्नियर कैलिपर — आंतरिक जबड़े)

 

• The internal jaws are smaller, curved jaws at the top of the instrument, specifically designed to be inserted inside a hollow object to measure its internal diameter, such as that of a hollow cylinder, pipe, or ring.

 

• The external (main) jaws are used to measure the outer length/thickness of an object and the outer diameter of a rod or sphere.

 

• The thin depth rod/strip that extends from the end of the main scale is used separately to measure the depth of a hole, beaker, or cylindrical container.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A standard vernier calliper has a least count of 0.01 cm (0.1 mm), obtained by dividing the value of one main scale division by the total number of vernier scale divisions.

 

• Vernier callipers are widely used in engineering and laboratories for precise linear measurements, being more accurate than an ordinary ruler.

 

NOTE

 

• The length correct up to 1 mm (Option 1): This describes the coarser precision of an ordinary scale, not the specific function of the internal jaws.

 

• The depth of a beaker (Option 2): This is measured using the separate depth probe/rod, not the internal jaws.

 

• The length of a rod and diameter of a sphere (Option 3): These outer dimensions are measured using the external (main) jaws, not the internal jaws.

question: Tsang Po and Jamuna are other names of which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brahmaputra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Brahmaputra river is known by different names along its course through different countries. (त्सांगपो और जमुना — ब्रह्मपुत्र नदी)

 

• It originates near Mansarovar Lake in Tibet, where it is called Tsang Po (Yarlung Tsangpo).

 

• After entering India through Arunachal Pradesh, it is called the Dihang/Siang, and further downstream in Assam it is known as the Brahmaputra.

 

• On entering Bangladesh, it is called the Jamuna, where it eventually merges with the Ganga (Padma) before draining into the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmaputra is unique among major Indian rivers for being male-named ('son of Brahma') and for having a large mid-channel river island, Majuli, in Assam — one of the world's largest river islands.

 

• It is a transboundary river, flowing through Tibet (China), India, and Bangladesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Indus (Option 1): Known as the Sindhu, originates near Mansarovar too but flows northwest through Ladakh and Pakistan; not called Tsang Po or Jamuna.

 

• Ganga (Option 2): Originates from the Gangotri glacier and is called the Padma in Bangladesh, not the Jamuna.

 

• Narmada (Option 3): Originates at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows entirely within India; unrelated to Tsang Po or Jamuna.

question: What is the cost of the ‘Nand Baba Milk Mission’ scheme launched by the Uttar Pradesh state government in 2023 to provide milk producers the facility of selling their milk at a reasonable price in villages through dairy co-operative societies?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ₹1,000 crore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nand Baba Milk Mission was launched by the Uttar Pradesh state government in June 2023 at a cost of ₹1,000 crore. (नंद बाबा मिल्क मिशन — 1000 करोड़ रुपये)

 

• The scheme aims to strengthen the dairy sector by helping milk producers/farmers sell their milk at reasonable, fair prices in villages through dairy co-operative societies, cutting out exploitative middlemen.

 

• It seeks to boost milk procurement, processing capacity, and rural incomes, and is aligned with UP's aim of becoming a leading milk-producing and dairy-processing state.

 

• The scheme is named after Nand Baba, the foster father of Lord Krishna, reflecting Uttar Pradesh's cultural association with Krishna and cattle-rearing (Braj region).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uttar Pradesh is India's largest milk-producing state, and the scheme is part of the state's broader push to modernise its dairy value chain.

 

• The scheme complements central schemes like the National Programme for Dairy Development (NPDD) and Rashtriya Gokul Mission.

 

NOTE

 

• ₹500 crore (Option 1): Understates the actual announced outlay of the scheme.

 

• ₹1,500 crore (Option 2): Not the figure associated with the Nand Baba Milk Mission.

 

• ₹2,000 crore (Option 3): Overstates the actual announced cost of ₹1,000 crore.

question: Medini Rai of Chanderi, Hasan Khan of Mewat and Mahmud Lodi joined Rana Sanga with their forces to fight against which of the following Mughal rulers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Babur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Medini Rai of Chanderi, Hasan Khan Mewati of Mewat, and Mahmud Lodi (son of Sikandar Lodi) joined Rana Sanga of Mewar in a confederacy to oppose Babur. (राणा सांगा और बाबर — खानवा का युद्ध)

 

• This combined force fought Babur at the famous Battle of Khanwa in 1527, near Fatehpur Sikri (Agra).

 

• Babur declared this battle a jihad and, after a hard-fought contest, decisively defeated the Rajput-Afghan confederacy, consolidating Mughal rule in North India after his earlier victory at Panipat (1526).

 

• Rana Sanga was wounded in the battle and died shortly after in 1528, marking a major setback for Rajput power in North India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Babur founded the Mughal Empire in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat (1526).

 

• Babur's other major battles include the Battle of Chanderi (1528) against Medini Rai and the Battle of Ghaghra (1529) against the Afghans and the Sultan of Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Akbar (Option 2): Fought later Rajput rulers, notably at the Battle of Haldighati (1576) against Maharana Pratap, not Rana Sanga.

 

• Aurangzeb (Option 3): Mughal ruler from 1658-1707, over a century after Rana Sanga's time.

 

• Humayun (Option 4): Babur's son and successor; famously lost his kingdom temporarily to Sher Shah Suri, unrelated to the Rana Sanga confederacy.

question: Which singer from Assam was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhupen Hazarika.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. Bhupen Hazarika, the legendary singer, lyricist, and filmmaker from Assam, was posthumously awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 2019. (भूपेन हजारिका — भारत रत्न 2019)

 

• Popularly called 'Sudhakantha', he is renowned for songs like 'Bistirno Parore' and for his contribution to Assamese, Bengali, and Hindi music and cinema.

 

• He had earlier received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1992) and the Padma Bhushan (2001).

 

• He passed away in 2011, and the Bharat Ratna was conferred posthumously along with Pranab Mukherjee and Nanaji Deshmukh in 2019.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhupen Hazarika composed and sang for films across languages and worked to popularise Assamese folk music internationally.

 

• Other Bharat Ratna awardees from the field of arts/music include M.S. Subbulakshmi, Bismillah Khan, and Lata Mangeshkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Padmanav Bordoloi (Option 1): Not a recipient of the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Rameshwar Pathak (Option 2): Not a recipient of the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Archana Mahanta (Option 3): A respected Assamese playback singer, but not a Bharat Ratna awardee.

question: Belur Math was founded by which of the following social reformers in British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Vivekanand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Belur Math, on the western bank of the Hooghly river near Kolkata, is the headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Ramakrishna Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1899. (बेलूर मठ — स्वामी विवेकानंद)

 

• It was established in memory of Vivekananda's guru, Ramakrishna Paramahansa, and serves as the spiritual and administrative centre of the Ramakrishna movement.

 

• Swami Vivekananda had earlier founded the Ramakrishna Mission itself in 1897, focused on social service, education, and the propagation of Vedanta philosophy.

 

• Belur Math's architecture is notable for blending Hindu, Christian, and Islamic styles, symbolising the unity of religions that Vivekananda preached.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Swami Vivekananda famously represented Hinduism at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893.

 

• National Youth Day in India is celebrated on 12 January, Swami Vivekananda's birthday.

 

NOTE

 

• RG Bhandarkar (Option 2): A noted Indologist and social reformer associated with the Prarthana Samaj, not the founder of Belur Math.

 

• VN Mandlik (Option 3): A Maharashtrian scholar and reformer, unrelated to the founding of Belur Math.

 

• KT Telang (Option 4): A jurist and reformer associated with the Prarthana Samaj and the Indian National Congress, not Belur Math.

question: ‘Castling’ is related to which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Castling is a special move in the game of Chess involving the king and either rook. (कैसलिंग — शतरंज)

 

• It is the only move in chess where a player moves two pieces (the king and a rook) at the same time, and it is used primarily to safeguard the king by moving it to a more protected position near a corner.

 

• Castling can only be performed if neither the king nor the chosen rook has moved previously, there are no pieces between them, and the king is not in check nor passes through a square attacked by an opponent's piece.

 

• Other chess-specific terms include 'checkmate', 'en passant', 'stalemate', and 'zugzwang'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chess terminology also includes 'Fool's Mate' and 'Scholar's Mate' for quick checkmates, and the Elo rating system used to rank player strength.

 

• India's Viswanathan Anand and Gukesh Dommaraju are prominent World Chess Champions from India.

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 1): Uses terms like 'let' and 'topspin'; castling is not associated with it.

 

• Billiards (Option 2): Uses terms like 'cannon' and 'break'; unrelated to castling.

 

• Tennis (Option 3): Uses terms like 'deuce', 'ace' and 'love'; castling is not a tennis term.

question: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gulzarilal Nanda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gulzarilal Nanda was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India, having served twice as acting Prime Minister for a combined total of only about 26 days. (गुलजारीलाल नंदा — सबसे कम समय तक प्रधानमंत्री)

 

• His first term was from 27 May to 9 June 1964 (13 days), following the death of Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

• His second term was from 11 to 24 January 1966 (13 days), following the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri in Tashkent.

 

• On both occasions he stepped in as caretaker until a new Prime Minister (Shastri, then Indira Gandhi) was elected by the Congress Parliamentary Party.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gulzarilal Nanda also served as a Union Cabinet Minister holding portfolios such as Labour, Planning, and Home Affairs.

 

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1997 for his contributions to public life.

 

NOTE

 

• Chandra Shekhar (Option 1): Served as Prime Minister for about 7 months (1990-91), longer than Nanda's terms.

 

• Charan Singh (Option 3): Served as Prime Minister for about 5-6 months (1979-80), also longer than Nanda's terms.

 

• Atal Bihari Vajpayee (Option 4): His first term in 1996 lasted 13 days, matching one of Nanda's individual terms, but Nanda's two combined terms make his total tenure the shortest overall.

question: Which of the following organisations is NOT a winner of the $100,000 cash prize as ‘Best Small Business: Good Food for All’, announced by the United Nations for providing inspiring, diverse and impactful solutions in improving access to healthy and sustainable food?
option_3: Oorja Development Solutions India Private Limited
solution_text:
The correct answer is Patanjali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The United Nations Food Systems Summit recognised 50 small businesses worldwide under the 'Best Small Business: Good Food for All' competition, sharing a total prize pool of $100,000. (सर्वश्रेष्ठ लघु व्यवसाय पुरस्कार — पतंजलि विजेता नहीं)

 

• Three India-based enterprises were among the winners: Edible Routes Private Limited (urban farming/local produce access), Oorja Development Solutions India Private Limited (solar-powered farming-as-a-service), and Taru Naturals (organic produce from tribal and small-scale farmers).

 

• Patanjali was not among the announced winners of this UN competition; it is a large, well-established consumer goods company rather than a small enterprise fitting the competition's eligibility criteria.

 

• The competition specifically targeted small businesses (with roughly 5-250 employees) working across the food value and supply chain to promote healthier, more sustainable and equitable food systems.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The competition ran under the umbrella of the UN Food Systems Summit 2021, aimed at transforming global food systems to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

 

• Winners were showcased at the Food Systems Pre-Summit held in Rome in July 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Edible Routes Private Limited (Option 2): A genuine Indian winner, providing urban dwellers access to locally grown fresh produce through farm allotments.

 

• Oorja Development Solutions India Private Limited (Option 3): A genuine Indian winner, offering solar energy solutions for agriculture as a service.

 

• Taru Naturals (Option 4): A genuine Indian winner, working with tribal and small-scale organic farmers across India.

question: At the 36th National Games, Hashika Ramchandra won six gold medals in which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swimming.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Hashika Ramchandra, a young swimmer, won six gold medals (out of seven total medals) in swimming at the 36th National Games, held in Gujarat in 2022. (36वें राष्ट्रीय खेल — हशिका रामचंद्र, तैराकी)

 

• She set meet records in multiple individual events, including the 200m freestyle, 200m butterfly, and 400m freestyle, and was also part of a record-setting relay team.

 

• For her outstanding performance, she was honoured with the 'Best Female Athlete' award at the Games, alongside swimmer Sajan Prakash, who won the Best Male Athlete award.

 

• The 36th National Games were notable for being held after a long gap due to the COVID-19 pandemic, with Services finishing atop the overall medal tally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sajan Prakash, an Olympic swimmer, was named Best Male Athlete at the same 36th National Games.

 

• The National Games are India's biggest multi-disciplinary domestic sporting event, held periodically among Indian states and union territories.

 

NOTE

 

• Boxing (Option 1): Not the sport in which Hashika Ramchandra competed at the Games.

 

• Wrestling (Option 2): Not associated with Hashika Ramchandra's medal haul.

 

• Badminton (Option 4): Not the sport she represented; she is a swimmer, not a badminton player.

question: Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is an eminent musician associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mridangam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman is a legendary Carnatic classical musician renowned as a Mridangam maestro. (उमयालपुरम के. शिवरामन — मृदंगम वादक)

 

• He has accompanied virtually every leading Carnatic vocalist and instrumentalist over a career spanning more than seven decades and is credited with popularising the mridangam on the international stage.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 2010, India's second-highest civilian award, in recognition of his contribution to classical music.

 

• The mridangam is a classical South Indian percussion (drum) instrument, considered the primary rhythmic accompaniment in Carnatic music concerts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other renowned mridangam players include Palghat Mani Iyer and Karaikudi Mani.

 

• Carnatic music, the classical music tradition of South India, typically features instruments like the veena, violin, mridangam, and ghatam.

 

NOTE

 

• Sitar (Option 1): A Hindustani (North Indian) stringed instrument famously played by Pandit Ravi Shankar, not associated with Sivaraman.

 

• Guitar (Option 2): A Western stringed instrument, unrelated to Sivaraman's classical Carnatic career.

 

• Dhol (Option 3): A folk percussion instrument common in Punjab and North India, different from the classical mridangam Sivaraman plays.

question: Which of the following ports was developed as a Satellite port to relieve the pressure at the Mumbai port?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru Port.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jawaharlal Nehru Port (also known as Nhava Sheva Port), located across the harbour from Mumbai in Maharashtra, was developed as a satellite port to relieve congestion and pressure at the older Mumbai (Bombay) Port. (जवाहरलाल नेहरू बंदरगाह — मुंबई बंदरगाह का दबाव कम करने हेतु)

 

• Commissioned in 1989, it is today India's largest container port, handling a major share of the country's containerised cargo traffic.

 

• It is a major port under the direct administrative control of the Government of India, situated on the Arabian Sea coast.

 

• The development of JNPT reflected the need for a modern, deep-draft container terminal as Mumbai's original port infrastructure became increasingly congested with rising trade volumes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India currently has 13 major ports, including Kolkata, Chennai, Kochi, Visakhapatnam, Paradip, and Kandla (Deendayal Port), besides JNPT and Mumbai Port.

 

• JNPT has since been renamed Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA).

 

NOTE

 

• New Mangalore Port (Option 1): A major port in Karnataka, not developed to relieve Mumbai port's pressure.

 

• Marmagao Port (Option 2): A major port in Goa, primarily known for iron ore exports, unrelated to Mumbai's congestion.

 

• Deendayal Port Authority (Option 3): Formerly Kandla Port in Gujarat, an independent major port, not a satellite of Mumbai port.

question: In which of the following situations does the government run a deficit budget?
option_1: When the government expenditure and revenue both are zero.
option_2: When the government expenditure exceeds revenue.
option_3: When the government expenditure equals revenue.
option_4: When the government revenue exceeds expenditure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is When the government expenditure exceeds revenue.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A deficit budget occurs when the government's total expenditure exceeds its total revenue in a given financial year. (घाटे का बजट — व्यय, राजस्व से अधिक)

 

• To finance this gap, the government has to resort to borrowing (domestic or external) or draw down its reserves, which adds to public debt.

 

• Deficit budgets are common in developing economies like India, which need higher spending on infrastructure, welfare schemes, and development, often exceeding tax and non-tax revenue collections.

 

• Key deficit indicators in India's budget include the fiscal deficit, revenue deficit, and primary deficit, each measuring a different aspect of the expenditure-revenue gap.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A balanced budget is when expenditure equals revenue, and a surplus budget is when revenue exceeds expenditure.

 

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003, sets targets to control and reduce India's fiscal deficit over time.

 

NOTE

 

• Expenditure and revenue both zero (Option 1): Describes an unrealistic scenario with no budget activity at all, not a deficit.

 

• Expenditure equals revenue (Option 3): This describes a balanced budget, not a deficit budget.

 

• Revenue exceeds expenditure (Option 4): This describes a surplus budget, the opposite of a deficit budget.

question: Rottela Panduga or the Roti Festival is celebrated in which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rottela Panduga, also called the Roti Festival, is celebrated in Nellore district of Andhra Pradesh. (रोत्तेला पंडुगा / रोटी उत्सव — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• The festival is held at the Dargah of Hazrat Syed Ibrahim Shaheed in Nellore, where devotees offer rotis (flatbreads) as a mark of devotion and gratitude, believing this fulfils their wishes.

 

• It is celebrated by people across religious communities — Hindus and Muslims alike — symbolising communal harmony, and is one of the most prominent local fairs of the region.

 

• The festival's origins are linked to a local legend of the Sufi saint Hazrat Ibrahim, and it typically features a large fair alongside the ritual offering of roti.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Andhra Pradesh also hosts other notable regional festivals like Ugadi (Telugu New Year) and the Tirupati Brahmotsavam.

 

• Similar syncretic festivals celebrating communal harmony are found across India, reflecting India's composite culture.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Known for festivals like Mysuru Dasara, not Rottela Panduga.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): Known for festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi, not Rottela Panduga.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 4): Known for festivals like Pongal, not Rottela Panduga.

question: In the context of Mathura school of Art, during which of the following periods were a number of sculptures of Brahmanical deities, such as Kartikeya, Vishnu and Kubera carved?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kushana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mathura school of Art flourished most prominently under the Kushana period, when numerous sculptures of Brahmanical deities such as Kartikeya, Vishnu, and Kubera were carved. (मथुरा कला शैली — कुषाण काल)

 

• The Mathura school used spotted red sandstone and, unlike the Gandhara school, was an indigenous Indian style not influenced by Greek/Hellenistic art.

 

• It flourished under the patronage of the Kushana ruler Kanishka, and produced the earliest anthropomorphic images of the Buddha alongside Hindu and Jain deities, reflecting its multi-religious character.

 

• Mathura sculptures are characterised by fuller, more robust and life-like figures compared to the more Hellenistic-influenced Gandhara style.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gandhara school of Art, contemporaneous with Mathura, also flourished under Kushana patronage but was heavily influenced by Greco-Roman styles (Indo-Greek fusion).

 

• The Amaravati school of Art in the Krishna-Godavari delta developed under Satavahana patronage using white marble.

 

NOTE

 

• Shaka (Option 1): A dynasty that ruled parts of western/northwestern India but is not specifically credited with these Mathura Brahmanical carvings.

 

• Parthian (Option 2): Ruled briefly in northwestern India before the Kushanas; not associated with this phase of Mathura art.

 

• Satavahana (Option 3): Patronised the Amaravati school of art in the Deccan/South India, not the Mathura school.

question:
Match the terms in column A with their respective properties in column B.

Column-A

i. Glucose

ii. Yeast

iii. Glycolysis

iv. Pyruvic acid

Column-B

a. Intermediate substance in breakdown of glucose

b. Glucose is converted into pyruvic acid

c. Uses nutrients for fermentation process

d. Best organic substrate for respiration
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• These four terms are correctly matched based on the biochemistry of cellular respiration and fermentation. (कोशिकीय श्वसन — ग्लूकोज, यीस्ट, ग्लाइकोलिसिस, पाइरुविक अम्ल)

 

• Glucose (i) is the 'best organic substrate for respiration' (d), being the primary sugar molecule oxidised by cells to release energy.

 

• Yeast (ii) is a micro-organism that 'uses nutrients for the fermentation process' (c), converting sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide under anaerobic conditions.

 

• Glycolysis (iii) is the metabolic pathway in which 'glucose is converted into pyruvic acid' (b), occurring in the cytoplasm and yielding a net gain of 2 ATP molecules.

 

• Pyruvic acid (iv) is the 'intermediate substance in the breakdown of glucose' (a), formed at the end of glycolysis and further processed in aerobic respiration (Krebs cycle) or fermentation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Aerobic respiration fully oxidises pyruvic acid via the Krebs cycle and electron transport chain to produce up to 36-38 ATP molecules, using oxygen.

 

• Anaerobic respiration/fermentation converts pyruvic acid into ethanol and CO₂ (in yeast) or lactic acid (in muscle cells), yielding far less energy than aerobic respiration.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-b, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c): Wrongly assigns 'glucose converted into pyruvic acid' to glucose itself and 'best substrate' to glycolysis.

 

• Option 3 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Wrongly assigns the 'intermediate substance' description to glucose and 'best substrate' to pyruvic acid.

 

• Option 4 (i-b, ii-d, iii-a, iv-c): Wrongly assigns 'best organic substrate' to yeast and 'fermentation' to pyruvic acid.

question: As per the UNDP, the rank of Sri Lanka in the Human Development Index (2022) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 73/189.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the UNDP Human Development Report for the year 2022, Sri Lanka was ranked 73rd out of 189 countries on the Human Development Index (HDI). (मानव विकास सूचकांक 2022 — श्रीलंका, रैंक 73)

 

• This placed Sri Lanka in the 'High Human Development' category, with an HDI value reflecting relatively strong performance on health, education, and standard-of-living indicators.

 

• The HDI is a composite index computed from three dimensions: life expectancy at birth, expected and mean years of schooling, and Gross National Income (GNI) per capita.

 

• The HDI is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) as part of its Human Development Report.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Norway, Switzerland, and Ireland have consistently ranked among the top countries on the HDI in recent years.

 

• India ranked 132nd in the 2022 HDI report, placed in the 'Medium Human Development' category.

 

NOTE

 

• 74/189 (Option 1): Close to, but not the actual figure reported for Sri Lanka.

 

• 75/189 (Option 3): Not the correct rank as per the 2022 HDI report.

 

• 72/189 (Option 4): Not the correct rank as per the 2022 HDI report.

question: If a bar magnet is hung from a string, in which direction does its north pole point?
solution_text:
The correct answer is North.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• If a bar magnet is freely suspended (hung from a string) so it can rotate, its north pole always points towards the geographic North direction. (छड़ चुंबक — उत्तर दिशा)

 

• This happens because the Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet, with its magnetic south pole located near the geographic North, which attracts the north-seeking pole of the freely suspended magnet.

 

• This principle is the basis for the working of a magnetic compass, which has been used for navigation for centuries.

 

• The pole of a freely suspended magnet that points north is therefore called the 'north-seeking pole', and the one pointing south is the 'south-seeking pole'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Like poles repel and unlike poles attract — this is a fundamental law of magnetism.

 

• Earth's magnetic north pole is actually located close to its geographic South pole in terms of magnetic polarity, which is why a compass's north-seeking needle points to geographic North.

 

NOTE

 

• West (Option 1): Not the direction indicated by a freely suspended magnet's north pole.

 

• East (Option 3): Not the direction indicated by a freely suspended magnet's north pole.

 

• South (Option 4): This is the direction the magnet's south pole points to, not its north pole.

question: Fugdi dance is associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fugdi is a traditional folk dance form associated with the state of Goa. (फुगड़ी नृत्य — गोवा)

 

• It is typically performed by women, especially during Hindu festivals like Ganesh Chaturthi, and involves rhythmic clapping and singing without any musical instruments.

 

• Dancers move in a circular pattern, often increasing in speed, while singing folk songs that narrate stories, myths, or express devotion.

 

• Fugdi is deeply rooted in Goan rural culture and is performed as a community activity, particularly by women of the Hindu community.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Goa include Dhalo, Dekhni, and Zagor.

 

• Goa is also known for the Shigmo festival, a spring festival featuring vibrant folk dance and music performances.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 2): Known for folk dances like Langvir Nritya and Chholiya, not Fugdi.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Raslila and Kajri, not Fugdi.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Known for classical/folk forms like Kathakali and Theyyam, not Fugdi.

question: Which of the following groups/parties was started in San Francisco, United States of America during the Indian National Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghadar Party.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco, United States of America, by Lala Har Dayal, along with Sohan Singh Bhakna as its first president. (गदर पार्टी — सैन फ्रांसिस्को, अमेरिका)

 

• It was formed by Indian immigrants, largely Punjabi settlers on the West Coast of the USA and Canada, with the aim of overthrowing British rule in India through armed revolution.

 

• The party published a newspaper called 'Ghadar' (meaning 'revolt/mutiny') to spread revolutionary ideas among Indians settled abroad.

 

• Members attempted to organise an uprising in India, notably the failed Ghadar Mutiny/Conspiracy of 1915, coinciding with World War I.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ghadar Party later merged its efforts with other revolutionary movements and figures such as the Berlin Committee and the Indo-German Conspiracy during World War I.

 

• Prominent Ghadarites included Kartar Singh Sarabha, executed at the young age of 19 for his revolutionary activities.

 

NOTE

 

• Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (Option 1): Founded in India in 1928 by Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh, not in the USA.

 

• Swaraj Party (Option 2): Founded in 1923 in India by Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan Das, not abroad.

 

• Khilafat Committee (Option 3): Founded in India in 1919 by the Ali Brothers to protest the treatment of the Ottoman Caliph, not in San Francisco.

question: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Certiorari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The writ of Certiorari is issued by a higher court (High Court or Supreme Court) to a lower court, tribunal, or quasi-judicial authority that has already decided a case in excess of its jurisdiction, in order to quash that order. (सर्टिओरारी रिट — क्षेत्राधिकार से अधिक निर्णय को रद्द करना)

 

• It is a curative/corrective writ, issued after the lower court or authority has passed its order, to correct an excess or abuse of jurisdiction already committed.

 

• The literal meaning of 'Certiorari' is 'to be certified' or 'to be informed', reflecting its purpose of calling up the records of a case for review.

 

• It is closely related to, but distinct from, the writ of Prohibition, which is preventive rather than corrective in nature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The five writs recognised under Articles 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution are: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.

 

• Certiorari can be issued against judicial, quasi-judicial, and (since some landmark judgments) certain administrative authorities as well.

 

NOTE

 

• Quo Warrant(o) (Option 1): Issued to question the legal authority of a person holding a public office, unrelated to jurisdictional excess by a court.

 

• Habeas Corpus (Option 2): Issued to produce a detained person before the court to check the legality of their detention, unrelated to this scenario.

 

• Prohibition (Option 4): A preventive writ issued to stop a lower court from proceeding with a case that exceeds its jurisdiction before it passes its final order, unlike Certiorari which corrects an order already passed.
